Hi Sabrina —

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap and next steps on the Mutual Action Plan (attached: acme_MAP_v1.xlsx) with a focus on the performance/load milestone we discussed.

Summary of the MAP milestone we want to lock down for the load/perf test:
- Milestone: Traffic replay load test (production traffic replay)
- Objective: Validate peak QPS handling and latency SLOs under production-shaped load; verify dedicated capacity sizing for steady-state and burst.
- Target close date for milestone: 2026-02-28 (aim for test window before end of month)
- Responsible: Acme: provide traffic capture and test account; Redwood: run replay on staging/dedicated pool, provide results and sizing recommendation.
- Dependencies: traffic capture export (CSV or PCAP), baseline nomination for peak QPS (today you mentioned ~800 peak QPS), test data scrubbing, and a sandbox account with similar dataset.

Proposed test scope options (pick one):
A) Full traffic replay (recommended) — replay 24-hour production window with peak windows scaled to observed peak. Redwood will provision a dedicated test pool sized to expected peak and run multiple iterations.
B) Targeted peak windows — replay only 2 hours around peak traffic to validate peak QPS response and auto-scaling behavior. Faster, less costly.

Suggested test windows (PST):
- Wed 2026-02-24 18:00–22:00 PST (preferred)
- Thu 2026-02-25 02:00–06:00 PST (backup)

Can you confirm:
1) Which scope (A or B) you prefer?
2) Confirm peak QPS number and whether 800 is the right estimate.
3) Confirm you can share the traffic capture file and whether Jake or someone from infra will provide the sanitized export by EOD 2026-02-17.

I'll loop in Marissa (SE) and Camila (CS) to handle the replay orchestration and capacity sizing. Once we confirm scope and get the capture, Marissa will propose the exact dedicated pool size and cost/estimate for the test run.

Thanks —

Hi all — thanks for the details. Quick plan and preliminary sizing below.

Planned replay: Full 24-hour production-shaped replay, scaled to Acme's observed peak QPS (800). We'll run three iterations (dry run, full run, validation run).

Preliminary sizing (estimate):
- Target latency profile: 95th pct <= 350ms for generation calls under 800QPS
- Instance type recommend: 8x A100s (or equivalent DGX-class instances) in a dedicated pool for steady-state + headroom for bursts.
- Estimated concurrent inference slots: ~1200 slots (based on token sizes and average request concurrency)
- Test duration: ~6 hours active replay per iteration (we'll bin traffic; replay can be compressed to only active windows), total wall time including setup: ~10 hours.
- Estimated cost for test runs (infra-only): ~$9k–$12k per full iteration (depends on compression and batching).

Dependencies (action items):
- Acme: provide sanitized traffic CSV by EOD 2026-02-17 (Jake) — include timestamps, request payload size, endpoint types, and peak window markers.
- Acme: provide a sandbox API key or test tenant with representative data (read-only credentials).
- Redwood: require a short maintenance window (we'll coordinate) and a point-of-contact to validate test outputs live.

Next steps:
1) Jake uploads sanitized capture to Drive link (or shares S3 pointer).
2) Marissa will turn this into a replay plan and provide a final dedicated pool sizing + cost estimate by 2026-02-17 morning.
3) Schedule the first dry run on Wed 2026-02-24 18:00 PST (tentative) — confirm by 2026-02-18.

I'll attach a brief replay checklist into the MAP doc and update the milestone row with responsibilities and expected close date.

Thanks —
